query:
package.json includes @nestjs/config, @nestjs/axios and axios.

User: I want to see the outgoing HTTP calls my app makes.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-http.md. Offer nest-profiler-http and apply the central gotcha: NOTHING is captured unless an instrumentation is listed — HttpCollectorModule.forRoot({ instrumentations: [AxiosInstrumentation] }) with AxiosInstrumentation imported from '@eleven-labs/nest-profiler-http/axios', and HttpModule imported in the SAME module. Must NOT claim capture is automatic with an empty instrumentations array.

query:
package.json includes @nestjs/config, class-validator and class-transformer. main.ts already contains app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true })).

User: Add DTO validation profiling.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-validator.md. Offer nest-profiler-validator, app-owned: with the dev-dependency install, add a validationPipe hook to the shared bootstrap — production main.ts keeps a plain ValidationPipe, main-dev.ts passes options => createProfilerValidationPipe(createClassValidatorPipe(options)) (createClassValidatorPipe, not a bare ValidationPipe, so per-property violations reach the panel); with the ConditionalModule install, wrap the pipe in main.ts unconditionally. Register the panel with ValidatorCollectorModule.forRoot() in the ProfilingModule bundle. Only one global validation pipe. Note DTOs need value imports (not 'import type').

query:
package.json includes @nestjs/config and nest-commander. The app has both an HTTP server (main.ts) and a CLI entrypoint (cli.ts using CommandFactory.run).

User: I want to profile my CLI commands and see them in the profiler UI.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-simple.md. Offer nest-profiler-commander and apply the cross-process gotcha: CLI and HTTP are separate processes, so set storageType: 'file' (or the SQLite adapter) on the core; register CommanderCollectorModule.forRoot() in the CLI bundle AND in the web bundle. With the dev-dependency install, the CLI gets its own entry: cli.ts keeps the profiler-free CliModule, cli-dev.ts runs CliDevModule (CliModule + CLI bundle) and passes logger: createProfilerLogger(...) to CommandFactory.run. With the ConditionalModule install, the CLI root module must import ConfigModule.forRoot(). Recommend adding .profiler/ to .gitignore.

query:
package.json includes @nestjs/config, @nestjs/graphql, @nestjs/apollo and graphql.

User: Add GraphQL profiling.
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-simple.md. Offer nest-profiler-graphql with GraphQLCollectorModule.forRoot() (the module is GraphQLCollectorModule, NOT ProfilerGraphQLModule) alongside GraphQLModule. Apply the gotcha: the GraphQLModule context MUST expose the request — for Apollo, context: ({ req }) => ({ req }). May suggest composing the core ignoreRequest with combineFilters(ignoreGraphQLPlayground, ignoreGraphQLIntrospection).

query: Does the TypeORM collector need inject: [DataSource]?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-orm.md. Answer: NO. TypeOrmCollectorModule self-resolves the DataSource via getDataSourceToken(connectionName), so forRoot() works with no inject. Use forRootAsync only to drive options (e.g. slowThreshold) from ConfigService, and pass connectionName for a non-default DataSource. Place it after TypeOrmModule.

query: Should the config and validator collectors go in the root module or a feature module?
expected_behavior: Must read collectors-matrix.md. Answer: neither — every collector, config and validator included, goes in the ProfilingModule bundle, since collectors resolve what they instrument across the whole app (DiscoveryService, connection tokens, global patches). With the dev-dependency install the bundle is loaded by main-dev.ts only; with the ConditionalModule install one gate on the bundle covers them all (a collector may also sit next to its host module with its own gate). The validator's pipe stays app-owned in the bootstrap.

query:

expected_behavior: Must read collectors-simple.md. Offer nest-profiler-event-emitter with EventEmitterCollectorModule.forRoot() in the ProfilingModule bundle; the app keeps EventEmitterModule.forRoot() in its own module. Explain the three surfaces: the Events panel on the emitting profile, the Discover / Events view, and one `event` profile per @OnEvent execution (profileListeners, on by default). Must flag the request-scoped-subscriber limitation and that @OnEvent suppresses handler errors by default.
